answer: In the orchard of decentralized systems, dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect punishment matrices provide a garden of security against Sybil multiplication, fostering a spiral of cooperation among honest agents, as the latter can derive a strictly positive expected payoff from participation, while the former can expect a strictly negative payoff from attempting to manipulate, thus establishing a Nash equilibrium where the expected utility of honest agents outweighs that of malicious ones.
